transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (CISO, CareBridge), Tom Reynolds (Head of Platform), Dr. Luis Moreno (Clinical Data Privacy)

Summary (auto): Quick security and privacy review focused on prompt/content retention, PII/PHI handling, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data. Discussed hosted vs private/VPC options for PHI workloads and next steps to share SOC 2 and KMS docs.

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Sophie from Redwood, i have Marco, our SE, with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Aisha: Hi Sophie, doing well, thanks. We wanted to run through a couple of things — primarily PHI handling and retention policy — and validate that Redwood's platform meets our compliance bar.
[00:20] Sophie: Absolutely. We've got a rough agenda: SOC 2/ISO coverage, RBAC and SSO, audit logs and retention, encryption at rest/in transit and KMS, data residency, and then prompt/response retention and training policies. Anything else?
[00:30] Tom: Also want to understand VPC/private deployment options since we may route PHI through a private deployment.
[00:40] Marco: Great, we'll cover hosted and private differences; we typically recommend Private for regulated PHI, but hosted can work with strict controls depending on use.

[02:05] Sophie: Starting with SOC 2 — Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report, and we also maintain ISO 27001 for our control environment. i'll share the artifacts after the call. note the SOC2 scope is for the Redwood hosted control plane and the inference runtime; private deployments have a different scope for customer-managed components.
[02:35] Aisha: When you say different scope, do you mean Redwood doesn't cover on-prem components? We need clarity for audits.
[02:42] Marco: Right — for Private/VPC, customer-managed infra (e.g., their own KMS, networking) is out of scope for Redwood's SOC2 since it's under the customer's control. We'll provide guidance and a runbook for what to include in their audit evidence.

[05:12] Dr. Moreno: Can you confirm data residency options? Our data must stay in EU and some records in a US backup region.
[05:20] Sophie: We support routing and region pinning. For hosted, you can choose region endpoints; for Dedicated/Private we can provision in target regions. We'll need to confirm exact regions and whether backups are allowed cross-region.

[07:00] Tom: Encryption — at rest and in transit — details? KMS? HSM?
[07:08] Marco: All customer content is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest. We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations — you can bring your own key (BYOK). For private deployments you can integrate with HSM/KMS in your network. I'll send the KMS integration guide which has examples for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault.
[07:40] Aisha: Is key rotation supported and can we audit key usage?
[07:45] Marco: Yes, key rotation is supported; audit logs show key usage events which are forwarded to the audit log pipeline. There's some nuance on hosted vs private for how keys are stored.

[10:10] Sophie: On RBAC and SSO — we support SAML2.0/SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC in the console. You can restrict who can create model endpoints, view logs, or change retention policies.
[10:35] Tom: SCIM user provisioning — does the provisioning create service accounts or just user identities?
[10:40] Marco: Both patterns are supported; we have guidance for creating dedicated service principals for programmatic access.

[12:50] Aisha: Audit logs — retention and export? We must retain logs for 7 years for certain events.
[12:58] Sophie: Audit logs can be configured to export to your S3/GCS/Azure blob with lifecycle policies. Retention on the Redwood console is configurable, but for long-term archiving you'll export to your storage. We also have log hashing for tamper evidence.

[15:20] Dr. Moreno: OK let's get into prompt/content retention and training. This is our big ask: do you retain prompt/response content, and will it be used to train Redwood's models?
[15:34] Marco: Short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to retrain our public models. We have a clear privacy policy and contractual language — i will read the clause: 'Redwood will not use customer-provided data to train or improve third-party or public models without explicit opt-in.'
[15:50] Tom: How about telemetry or aggregated stats?
[15:53] Marco: We do collect telemetry for platform operations (latency, error rates) but that's aggregated and doesn't contain raw full prompts. For hosted customers who opt into analytics, there's an opt-in toggle — but even then it's sanitized and aggregated.
[16:20] Aisha: How long are prompts retained? We need a retention window and an option to purge.
[16:25] Marco: Default retention for hosted is 30 days for logs and request/response payloads, with options to shorten or set to zero. For Dedicated/Private you control retention; we can set retention to zero and stream to your archive only. We'll include these options in the doc.

[18:40] Sophie: We should clarify PHI/PII handling — if you send PHI to hosted endpoints, you'll need either a Private deployment or ensure contractual protections and logging. We typically recommend Private for regulated PHI because you control key management and network isolation.
[19:05] Aisha: So For PHI we need to go Private — is that mandatory?
[19:10] Marco: It's not a legal mandate from Redwood but a best-practice. Some customers handle PHI in hosted with strict controls and BAAs; Redwood can sign a BAA for enterprise plans and enable additional controls. But for maximum isolation, Private/VPC is recommended.

[21:30] Dr. Moreno: About 'no training' confirmation — can you provide contractual language? We need an explicit representation that data will not be used to improve models.
[21:40] Sophie: Yes, we include a clause in the DPA/TOU that customer content will not be used for model training without consent. We'll attach the exact language.
[21:55] Tom: Any exceptions for safety or abuse detection?
[22:00] Marco: We may process telemetry for abuse detection, but that processing is designed to avoid storing raw prompts. If we ever need raw content for safety investigations, we'd follow a strict internal process and we'd notify the customer — and such use is covered by contract.

[24:25] Aisha: Do you have a way to redact or mask PHI automatically before it leaves our network?
[24:33] Marco: There's a client-side SDK feature for local redaction and a server-side pre-processing filter that can mask PII/PHI based on regex and named-entity detection. For high-sensitivity workloads we recommend client-side redaction prior to sending.

[27:00] Sophie: Let's talk about incident response and breach notification SLA.
[27:08] Marco: Our incident response playbook includes notify within 72 hours for confirmed breaches affecting customer data; we provide incident reports and remediation steps. For Dedicated/Private customers we can offer customized SLAs.

[29:10] Aisha: What about customer audit access: can we get evidence for a SOC 2 audit?
[29:18] Sophie: Yes, we provide standard evidence packages and coordinate with your auditors. For Private deployments, some evidence will come from your infra. We'll provide a mapping document that shows which controls are Redwood's vs customer-managed.

[31:45] Tom: Networking specifics — IP allowlisting, egress control, and split-horizon DNS?
[31:52] Marco: We support IP allowlisting and can configure egress rules in Private. For hosted we have managed egress and you can use private endpoints or VPC peering where supported. We'll share network diagrams and a checklist.

[34:10] Dr. Moreno: A few quick clarifying q's on logging: are prompts included in audit logs?
[34:18] Marco: By default prompts are part of request logs for a short retention window; audit logs capture metadata (who, when, endpoint) and not full payloads unless you enable full request logging. You can disable request payload logging and rely on metadata only.

[36:00] Aisha: Regarding deletion — if we request deletion of historical prompts, what is the process?
[36:06] Marco: We'll run a purge job that deletes payloads from live storage and from backups subject to backup retention windows; for hosted we guarantee purge within configured timeframe (we will include the exact SLAs in the doc). For Dedicated/Private you control backup retention and purge.

[38:20] Tom: Are there any data residency limitations for Private? like hardware procurement time?
[38:25] Sophie: Private provisioning lead times depend on region and capacity; we'll provide timelines. For Dedicated we have reserved capacity options.

[40:00] Aisha: A few customers ask about model provenance — which open models are used, and how do you ensure quantized or finetuned variants don't leak training data?
[40:12] Marco: We publish a model catalog showing base models and any Redwood-verified variants; we do not fine-tune on customer prompts. For proprietary model concerns we'll provide provenance docs.

[42:10] Sophie: Quick recap of action items and next steps: i'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts; Marco will send KMS/HSM integration guide and redaction SDK examples; CareBridge to confirm residency and whether they want a BAA; schedule follow-up private-deployment demo.
[42:30] Aisha: That works. Appreciate the clarity.
[42:38] Tom: We'll review the docs and follow up with a list of legal questions.
[42:45] Sophie: Great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up by end of week with the docs.
[42:55] Meeting end.
